_readme: Three sites in a multi-centre study. Each site holds its own operations corpus; documents never leave the site. Passages are written so that every planted conflict is decidable by exactly one mechanism, letting you show which layer fired. 'gold' is the answer key - do not ship it to clients.

passages.text: Following enrolment, participants enter the observation phase. Vital signs are recorded by the assigned nurse at each interval.
The minimum monitoring interval during the observation phase is 4 hours. Shorter intervals may be used at clinical discretion.
This version of the protocol takes effect on 2026-01-15 and supersedes all previously circulated observation schedules.
Concurrent anticoagulant therapy is permitted for participants already stabilised on a maintenance dose prior to enrolment.
Plasma specimens are held in refrigerated storage until the daily courier collection at 16:00.
Specimen storage category for plasma is refrigerated. Frozen storage is reserved for the long-term archive.
Where a participant deteriorates outside scheduled review, the matter is referred without delay to the on-call consultant, who holds decision authority.
Nursing staff should document the referral in the participant record at the time it is made, not retrospectively.
The observation ward operates with a nurse-to-participant ratio of 1 to 6 on day shifts.
Night shift cover is provided by two registered nurses and one healthcare assistant.
Participants are reviewed on a fixed schedule throughout the observation phase, as set out below.
The minimum monitoring interval during the observation phase is 6 hours. Deviations must be logged.
Concurrent anticoagulant therapy is not permitted at any point during the observation phase, irrespective of prior stabilisation.
Where a participant's condition changes unexpectedly, the duty registrar assumes responsibility for the clinical decision.
Plasma specimens are kept under refrigeration pending transfer. Ambient storage is not acceptable for this analyte.
Transfer to the central laboratory occurs twice daily, at 11:00 and at 17:30.
The observation ward runs a nurse-to-participant ratio of 1 to 6 across all day shifts.
Weekend staffing follows the weekday establishment with no reduction in registered nurse cover.
Participants are given a minimum of 24 hours to consider the information sheet before consent is sought.
A witnessed signature is required where the participant cannot read the information sheet unaided.
Local practice for the observation phase is described here for staff induction and does not replace the protocol.
Observations are taken at a minimum interval of 240 minutes during the observation phase, in line with the study protocol.
Concurrent anticoagulant therapy is permitted where a maintenance dose was established before enrolment.
The protocol version in force at this unit takes effect on 2026-03-01, following completion of local governance review.
Staff should not apply the schedule set out in earlier circulated drafts once the effective date has passed.
Plasma specimen storage category at this unit is frozen, owing to the distance from the central laboratory.
Specimens are batched and dispatched three times weekly rather than daily.
Unscheduled deterioration is escalated to the on-call consultant in the first instance.
The consultant may delegate to a senior registrar where the situation is judged stable.
New staff complete a half-day induction covering consent, observation practice and specimen handling.

gold._note: Each entry names the mechanism that SHOULD decide it. If a different layer fires, that is a bug worth showing.

conflicts.why: Plain numeric disagreement, same unit. Layer 1 must catch this with zero model involvement.
Version drift across sites. Date comparison, not semantics.
Polarity flip on a shared referent. Catchable without NLI if the extractor sets polarity correctly - this is the test of your extraction step, not your checker.
No numbers, no negation, near-zero lexical overlap. Layer 1 must ABSTAIN and hand this to NLI. This is the passage that justifies keeping a model in the loop.
Real conflict but NOT load-bearing. Under the default escalation policy this is detected and logged, not surfaced. Use it to demo that you are not spamming the human.

unit_trap.why: These AGREE, but only after unit normalisation. Un-normalised, the checker must abstain rather than report 4 vs 240 as a conflict. Silent false positives are how a safety tool loses trust; make the abstain visible in the demo, then add normalisation and watch it flip to corroborates.

corroborations.why: Agreement across sites. Must pass silently - no escalation.
Two of three sites agree; site-b is the outlier. Good material for showing majority context alongside the conflict rather than just a bare pair.

independent.why: consent_addendum (site-b) and induction (site-c) share no referent with anything else. Must produce no edges at all. If these generate pairs, your blocking is too loose.
